meta.name: reconcile
meta.description: 128 F-reconciliation (jav/reconcile.py): which bank statement line paid which incoming invoice, by code. The invoice types, the payment window, the signal thresholds, the payment channels, the pairs listed for their equal amount alone, the names learnt from a person's confirmations, the payment kinds left to a person and when a statement counts as verified coverage. Decisions: DECISIONS 128 (exact amount and at least one signal first; card payments with an exchange rate later; never 'unpaid'), DECISIONS 131.

changelog.note: 131 (DECISIONS 131): invoice_fields.payment_method; payment_channels (the postal cheque: an invoice payable by cheque and a line through a cheque payment app are tied by the payment_channel signal; patterns on the normalised, accent-free text, document vocabulary); amount_only (a line with exactly an invoice's amount in one currency, in its window, without a signal, is listed for a person, never proposed); learning.min_confirmations (a person's confirmation ties the line's counterparty name to the supplier, the learned_name signal; a payment app line teaches nothing).

130 K3: card payments of foreign-currency invoices (DECISIONS 128 variant C, second half). A forint line of a credit card statement and an invoice in another currency form a candidate when a signal ties them and the line falls in fx.window around the issue date; the invoice amount is converted at the MNB rate of the issue date (jav/fx.py) and the pair is proposed when the line is within policy.json reconcile.fx_tolerance. Without a known rate the pair is listed, not proposed (status rate_missing). The card accounts also count in the coverage of a foreign-currency invoice.

128 K1: first version. Rules ported selectively from the legacy project's orchestrator/framework/payables.py 0.1.1 (10_AIFLOW_V4 HEAD 4256cba): the reason-coded exclusions, the signals and 'an equal amount alone is no candidate'. New: the exact-amount rule, the window's upper end, coverage by verified statements.
